reuse.why: Builds on the existing getScheduledAmount and getApproxNumberThreshold and routes every server copy (forecast, posting, action sync, preview, budget template), the API model and the UI through them.

duplication.why: Removes five inline midpoint copies, but leaves the rule split across two overlapping exported helpers (getScheduledAmount for ranges, getExpectedAmount adding the approximate case) with near-identical names.

placement.why: The expected-amount rule lives in shared/schedules.ts, used by both server and desktop-client, and the API field is computed in the API model mapper.

scope.why: Changes all track the four requests, though the API field is typed via an ad-hoc intersection on toExternal and two release notes with inconsistent categories are added.

maintainability.why: One rule path for all consumers is easy to own, but having both getScheduledAmount and getExpectedAmount public invites callers to pick the wrong one, and expectedAmount is missing from APIScheduleEntity so 'api/schedules-get' consumers do not see it in the type.

bypasses_abstraction.where: No remaining call site computes the amount itself; useScheduleEdit uses getScheduledAmount only for operator switching.

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedAmount delegates to getScheduledAmount rather than copying it.

abstraction_drift.where: The approximate case is a wrapper branch in getExpectedAmount (shared/schedules.ts) layered on getScheduledAmount instead of a parameter on it; no call site bypasses the helpers.
